entry.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week
entry.summary: Every week the Stereogum staff chooses the five best new songs of the week. The eligibility period begins and ends Thursdays right before midnight. entry.content:
Every week the Stereogum staff chooses the five best new songs of the week. The eligibility period begins and ends Thursdays right before midnight. You can hear this week’s picks below and on Stereogum’s Favorite New Music Spotify playlist, which is updated weekly. (An expanded playlist of our new music picks is available to subscribers on Spotify and Apple Music, updated throughout the week.)

5

yeule - "Hystérique"

yeule has a penchant for otherworldly sounds. "Hystérique" is billed as "a post-apocalyptic cyborgian romance," and it's a hazy, buzzing whirlwind with a pulsing, infectious beat. yeule utters the names of designer brands in icy breaths and paints surreal, cinematic scenes: "Atomic electronic girl, crying in the rain/ Let's just dance, dance, dance, dance/ Dance away the pain." "Hystérique" sounds like a rave echoing from another a planet. —Danielle

4

The Healing Power Of Horses - "xstick_xstick"

The Healing Power Of Horses don't quite make sense. Two reclusive weirdos holed up in an attic in the English countryside who call themselves t and c, they make songs that unfold with the warped logic of an inside joke between two people who spend way, way too much time together. As c deadpans evocatively surreal nonsense in a coolly detached sing-song, "xstick_xstick" rides a fidgety earworm of a groove straight into the deepest recesses of your brain. What does any of it mean? Don't worry about it. Just hop in the saddle and be healed. —Peter

3

nowhere else to be - "r1 (ripples)"

The members of the Montreal group nowhere else to be choose to remain anonymous for now. That won't last. It can't. For one thing, these folks aren't hiding their faces in their videos or anything. More importantly, people want to know things about you when you make this kind of overwhelming tide of melody. "r1 (ripples)," with its walls of fuzz and its underwater keyboard glimmers, could be considered shoegaze, but there's a melodic swagger underneath that suggests something bigger. And when the singer gets into his lower register, the humanity shines through and stands out. He can't hide it. —Tom

2

Factory Floor - "Continuation"

How have Factory Floor returned after a decade away? With a burbling, squelching, strobing synth pulse and murmured vocals that rightly assume this beat is more than enough to sweep us away. If you can stop your body from twitching and grooving while "Continuation" is on, you've got more self control than me. "So let's begin the continuation." —Chris

1

Trinket - "If Not Soon Then Now"

Sometimes bitterness is a blink away from sweetness. And sometimes those volatile stakes make the sensations all the more delicious. Brooklyn’s Trinket capture the fragility that’s always hovering over something that’s too good to be true — a new relationship or fresh spark — on "If Not Soon Then Now." The melody is sugary and bright, almost Froot Loops-sweet, while the guitars carry a subtle grit, an undercurrent of fear or latent anxiety. Synths act as an extra glint, lending the track a certain dewy, early-morning shimmer — jangle pop at its finest. But isolated, the thorny guitar strums might almost register as an alarm. It’s a lovely tension between brightness and unease, a harmonious urgency, all glistening surfaces and something quietly trembling underneath. —Margaret

entry.title: bloodsports – “Ten Thousand Feet”
entry.summary: Last year, bloodsports unleashed their sufficiently eerie debut album Anything Can Be A Hammer, which earned them a spot on our list of the best new acts of 2025. We haven’t heard from the New York band since — until now. Today, just in time for Halloween, they’re back with a monster of a song…
entry.content:
Last year, bloodsports unleashed their sufficiently eerie debut album Anything Can Be A Hammer, which earned them a spot on our list of the best new acts of 2025. We haven't heard from the New York band since — until now. Today, just in time for Halloween, they're back with a monster of a song called "Ten Thousand Feet."

"'Ten Thousand Feet' was a very collaborative effort; we all wrote parts of it at different times or just by jamming out sections and putting it together as a group, so it feels very rewarding to have it finally out in the world especially after playing it live for the last year or so," the group explains. "Lyrically, this song is an attempt to explain a certain malaise or boredom that I was feeling at the time, and the sort of restless, unknowing, bird's-eye view anger that comes with that, referencing a story about a baseball player named Joe Sprinz, which we encourage everyone to read if they get the chance."

bloodsports, much like other Stereogum faves Truth Club, have a knack for capturing the creeping feeling of dread and stretching it out into an extensive, haunted house-like song. You never know what's around the corner, but you're just waiting for someone or something to jump out at you. The anticipation, though, is the most frightening part. Enter at your own risk below.

entry.content:
Doechii's Swamp Sessions blitz continues. Right now, the newly minted rap star is building up the release of an as-yet-unannounced album by dropping striking self-directed videos for the possibly-incomplete new songs "Bomb" and "Catwoman." Today, she shares "Lock Jaw," the most outrageous track to come out of this campaign yet.

"Lock Jaw" is a giddy, horny dance-rap attack that reminds me of Doechii's 2024 JT collab "Alter Ego." There's a bit of hyperpop in the spaced-out, fluffy pop chorus, but Doechii also gets into her deeply Southern Trina-style snarl-rap mode. The lightly NSFW video takes place at a party full of sex toys. The credits — there are credits — list Doechii as director and creative director and Taya Lee as co-director and movement director. Check it out below.

entry.content:
In 2024, Maxïmo Park released their eighth studio album Stream Of Life. Today, frontman Paul Smith is sharing "Lay Your Head Down," his first solo material in eight years.

"Lay Your Head Down" was co-produced with Field Music's David Brewis, and it features Kathryn Williams on vocals and Ed Cross on violin. "'Lay Your Head Down' is a pleading lullaby, written with my daughter in mind, but it applies to anyone who needs some peace of mind," Smith says. "I think it's one of the prettiest songs I've written, but there are a couple of darker moments hinting at disquiet."

The song is as fragile and serene as an acoustic ballad could be. Smith and Williams' voices weave together into hypnotic harmonies, and the beauty is heightened when the violin slowly seeps in. Listen below.

entry.content:
Esmeralda Road are a Belfast band that started out as Moonboot, until a streetwear brand of the same name made a fuss. In 2023, they won Single Of The Year at the NI Music Prize for their jazzy debut song "To U." They still don't have an album yet, but today they're sharing an evocative new ballad called "Here Honey."

"'Here Honey' is a song made in retaliation to all the distractions we are force fed day to day and how they eat away at our relationships with each other," the trio says. While they've incorporated elements of jazz and soul into their past tunes, "Here Honey" is pure emotional pop-rock. Watch the music video directed by Jay Whylie below.

He took part in entities like the Anticon Collective, cLOUDDEAD, Themselves, Subtle, 13 & God, and the Nevermen, moving further and further from regular underground rap circles all the while. entry.content:
In the late '90s, the Idaho-born linguistic maniac known as doseone helped pioneer a certain kind of skittery, moody avant-rap. He took part in entities like the Anticon Collective, cLOUDDEAD, Themselves, Subtle, 13 & God, and the Nevermen, moving further and further from regular underground rap circles all the while. But last year, doseone made a grand return, teaming up with present-day underground producer steel tipped dove on the Backwoodz Studioz album All Portrait, No Chorus. Now, doseone seems to be all the way back in.

Since the release of All Portrait, No Chorus, doseone has been in a prolific zone. He teamed up with Baltimore DIY great Height Keech for last year's Wood Teeth EP, then for a sequel earlier this year. Just last month, he released sighting, a full-length collab with producers Wino Willy and Zetroc. Now, doseone and steel tipped dove have made another album together, and now they've brought fellow rap weirdo Fatboi Sharif into the fold.

You should already know Fatboi Sharif, the prolific New Jersey rap iconoclast and onetime Stereogum Artist To Watch. Sharif releases music all the time, including collaborative records with Child Actor and ELUCID earlier this year. Sharif has worked with steep tipped dove many times over the years, and he and doseone make a perfectly natural pairing, their different kinds of jaggedness complementing each other. The resulting LP Truth Ugly is some real way-out shit, just as you'd expect. Check it out below.

entry.title: Rage Against The Machine & BTS Reportedly Turn Down Coachella; Dua Lipa, SZA, & Tame Impala “Nearly Confirmed”
entry.summary: Rumors have been swirling for a while now, but the people behind Coachella haven’t unveiled their 2027 lineup yet. (Last year, they announced the 2026 lineup in September.) Last month, we learned that Dua Lipa and Tame Impala were likely to headline next year’s festival, at least according to what sources told HITS Daily Double.…
entry.content:
Rumors have been swirling for a while now, but the people behind Coachella haven't unveiled their 2027 lineup yet. (Last year, they announced the 2026 lineup in September.) Last month, we learned that Dua Lipa and Tame Impala were likely to headline next year's festival, at least according to what sources told HITS Daily Double. Now, TMZ reports that those two acts are "nearly confirmed" as headliners, and so is SZA, one of the artists reportedly under consideration. TMZ also has some interesting reports on the acts who said no to Coachella.

According to TMZ, both Rage Against The Machine and BTS, two groups that don't otherwise have too much in common, both said no to headlining offers. Rage Against The Machine already headlined Coachella in 1999 and 2007, and they were booked to return in 2020, though that festival was obviously canceled for COVID reasons. RATM haven't played live since they finished their most recent reunion tour in 2022. K-pop has become an increasingly big deal at Coachella in recent years, but BTS have never played the festival before.

Past reports mentioned that Miley (formerly Cyrus) also turned down a Coachella offer and that Oasis and Radiohead were also being considered, though both of those seem like pretty big reaches. Instead, it looks like Coachella will have a set of three contemporary pop-star headliners. Tame Impala have already played Coachella four times, including a headlining set in 2019. SZA has played twice. Dua Lipa has never been on the festival bill. It's probably worth noting that Tame Impala has worked with both Dua Lipa and SZA. Earlier this month, Tame Impala and SZA guested, alongside King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, on Justice's Grand Theft Auto VI single "Flower In A Hurricane."

Next year's Coachella goes down Apr. 9-11 and then Apr. 16-18.

entry.title: 5 Thoughts On Olivia Rodrigo’s Unraveled Tour
entry.summary: Olivia Rodrigo’s Unraveled Tour rolled into Columbus last night for the first of two shows at Ohio State University’s Value City Arena. Five quick thoughts on that: 1. This week Rolling Stone put out its list of the 200 greatest rock songs of the 21st century so far. It’s ridiculous ragebait, but they weren’t wrong…
entry.content:
Olivia Rodrigo's Unraveled Tour rolled into Columbus last night for the first of two shows at Ohio State University's Value City Arena. Five quick thoughts on that:

1. This week Rolling Stone put out its list of the 200 greatest rock songs of the 21st century so far. It's ridiculous ragebait, but they weren't wrong to rank "good 4 u" so highly. Olivia Rodrigo is a rock artist at least as much as she's a pop artist. It was apparent on her tour supporting 2023's GUTS, which vacillated wildly between the guitar-powered explosions and bleeding-heart ballads. It's even more apparent on this tour, which follows June's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love. The setlist is a little more coherent, which is to say it mostly grouped its loud and quiet songs together into bunches. That meant the night began with eight straight high-energy numbers, most of them powered by booming drums and walls of guitar distortion, a few veering closer to the new wave vibes that factored into the new LP. Some trappings of a pop production remained. There were several outfit changes and video interludes. The stage was covered with fake flowers. She often sang directly into the camera. And in the night's biggest moment of pageantry, the climactic performance of "the cure" on the auxiliary stage concluded with water raining down on Rodrigo, washing one dress off her and revealing another. On the other hand, there was no choreography and no lip syncing. It was mostly just a powerful singer and her equally powerful band rocking out. She even crawled toward her guitarist at one point, then leaned back on her knees, reveling in the six-string heroics. It feels a little old-fashioned to praise a young woman for prioritizing rock over pop, especially coming from a fortysomething dad who attended the show with his daughter, so I'm not doing that. I'll just note that her creative output and professional associations keep growing in this direction, and that it's fun and interesting to have a figure like that in the mainstream.

2. Maybe it's because I saw You Can See Everything two nights earlier, but the performance of authenticity was on my mind. Rodrigo is still an entertainer first and foremost, and with that comes the performance of emotion. She smiles during the happy songs, looks distressed during the sad ones, gets her audience involved with sing-alongs and group scream sessions. The media-trained Disney Channel pedigree doesn't just go away, nor does the ingrained influence of that lady who sang about how she can do it with a broken heart. Rodrigo could be going through a personal crisis and we'd never know it because the show must go on. But I found her relative lack of ego interesting on Thursday night. A bunch of white confetti meant to resemble snow fell on her during "honeybee," the first in a stretch of ballads she performed seated at a piano late in the set. I was intrigued by her decision not to whisk the bits of paper out of her hair for the next two songs, to allow herself to appear less than flawless. Even more noteworthy was the decision to perform her last three songs with wet hair after the stunt in "the cure." You can end up in a recursive spiral trying to figure out whether she's doing this because she's beyond the bounds of artifice or because this is what someone beyond the bounds of artifice would do, but the fact is she did it when many of her peers would never dare.

3. Another thing many of her peers wouldn't try: playing a guitar solo. Rodrigo played instruments several times throughout the night, mostly just strumming a guitar or plinking out piano chords, but at the climax of "maggots for brains" she ripped off a Strokes-ish lead line she's been doing at all of her gigs lately. She's not exactly Annie Clark up there, but it's cool that she aspires to be, and even cooler that she risks flubbing it rather than waiting to try it until it comes off as naturally as the glory notes on "cigarette smoke." (By the way, those glory notes were glorious. Don't let this woman's hip credentials distract you from the fact that she can really sing.)

4. Rodrigo has not evolved as an artist so much that she needs to leave her teenage ballads behind, at least not yet. At 23, she's entering her mid-20s, which has me wondering how long her earliest material will hold up within the context of her evolving canon, especially the brokenhearted outpourings sung from a decidedly adolescent perspective. But those songs mostly still make sense in her live show for now. The SOUR cut "traitor," with its vitriol for an ex who found a new girlfriend suspiciously quickly, seemed maybe a pinch juvenile. But that album's deep cut "favorite crime" boasts one of the most potent climaxes in Rodrigo's catalog, when her voice shoots up to its highest range to lament, "All the things I did/ Just so I could call you mine/ All the things you did/ Well, I hope I was your favorite crime." Thursday night, that moment remained electrifying. She followed it with "drivers license," a song so huge that it somehow transcends my concerns about Rodrigo aging out of it. I can imagine her continuing to perform that one well into her old age as sort of youthful vignette, like Alex Chilton singing "Thirteen." Still, it was encouraging to see her close out the show with "expectations," the new wave "No Scrubs" that stands as her current single, teaching her young fans to maintain high standards rather than wallow in longing for a loser.

5. At the end of the show, Rodrigo put on a T-shirt supporting the campaign of Dr. Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor in Ohio. Earlier, she told us the best part of her day was mailing in her ballot. There was a voter registration table in the lobby. None of this was surprising because Rodrigo has regularly spoken out for causes she believes in. Her recent Daisy Chain Fields festival raised $20 million for women's rights organizations. She was present at Tom Morello's concert-as-political-rally a few weeks back. She could keep her show apolitical, but she's forcing her audience to reckon with issues that extend beyond personal love and heartbreak. You can't miss the activism, yet it doesn't drown out the entertainment value of her performance. If anything, the two components strengthen each other. They contribute to the sense that she's giving you, if not her whole self, at least her actual self. Good for her.

entry.title: Fire-Toolz – “Clustered Around My Opening!”
entry.summary: It has been a banner year for Angel Marcloid, the exciting and experimental Chicago musician who records as Fire-Toolz. Earlier this year, Fire-Toolz released Lavender Networks, a fascinatingly freewheeling album that combines glitched-out electronics with uncanny-valley pop, death metal screams, and a whole lot of other stuff that doesn’t seem like it should make sense…
entry.content:
It has been a banner year for Angel Marcloid, the exciting and experimental Chicago musician who records as Fire-Toolz. Earlier this year, Fire-Toolz released Lavender Networks, a fascinatingly freewheeling album that combines glitched-out electronics with uncanny-valley pop, death metal screams, and a whole lot of other stuff that doesn't seem like it should make sense together. It does, though. It's fucking awesome. After the album came out, Fire-Toolz remixed Wednesday and worked with past collaborator No Joy on the ridiculously strong EP Big Life, Big Leaf. Now, it's time for a new single.

At least for the moment, Fire-Toolz' new track "Cluster Around My Opening!" — what a title — is a one-off single. The track starts out feeling a bit like a vaporwave take on '80s synth-funk and Angelo Badalamenti soundtracks. But then, it's also got drum 'n' bass breakbeat ripples and head-exploding screamo vocals. The pile-up of different sounds and moods might leave you dizzy and exhausted, but that's the point. This is some true maximalist music. Listen below.

entry.content:
We're at the absolute height of spooky season right now, and now fanclubwallet have a new song about the scariest beastie that you might encounter this Halloween: The creep! Sorry to startle you. I know. I get scared thinking about them, too. But they're out there. Unlike so many other mythological varmints, creeps are unfortunately very real. If you're out in public, or maybe at your place of work, of them might be in the room with you right now! Hopefully, one of them isn't in your home. You need to look out for these creeps.

fanclubwallet, the Ottawa indie project led by Hannah Judge, released the album Living While Dying last year, right around Halloween. Earlier this year, fanclubwallet shared the one-off single "Moving Unison," and Judge's partner and collaborator Michael (Miki) Watson released their debut solo album Willow. "Creep-O," fanclubwallet's latest, is a muted garage-pop track about the people who just leave you feeling off. Judge says, "This song was created in basically one sitting. A feeling of weirdness was stuck with me, and I just had to get it out as quick as possible." Check it out below.

"Creep-O" is out now on Lauren Records.

entry.content:
A couple of months ago, the hardnosed Buffalo rap veteran released his one-off single "Summer '26," the latest in an annual series. Today, Benny's back with a new single called "Elevate." Technically, it's credited to both Benny and his Black Soprano Family crew, but Benny is the only one who raps on it.

On "Elevate," Benny talks frankly about his last few years moving into and then back out of the major-label system, making good money without ever moving out of harm's way. It's Benny in motivational hustle mode, and the beat, from producer Moose Tarantino, combines Southern rap boom with '80s-movie synths in ways that remind me of early Rick Ross. Check out the video below.

Benny's new Black Soprano Family compilation A Friend Of Ours 2 is out 11/13 on Perfect Time Music Group.

entry.content:
The newish NY/Nashville label Good English Records has been building a strong roster of rising bands, including Victoryland, Proun, Crate, face of an ancient gallery, and Billboard Style. Yesterday, New York duo Or Best Offer — Grace Schmidhauser and Brian Culligan — were the latest to join that marvelous family. They also released the lead single "Fast Strong Horse," from their forthcoming new album It Will Appear.

"Fast Strong Horse" is a wondrous ride. It begins with some electric drones, melancholic guitars, and somber vocals. Later, the song unravels with a stampede of percussion and brass embellishments. It's fucking sick. The song's title comes from the final lines of Clarice Lispector’s debut novel Near To The Wild Heart.

“This is sort of the record’s pop song, an attempt to summon sanity, agency and dignity during a period of feeling pathetic,” Schmidhauser explained in a press release. “It’s a quilt of associations created from the brain mush of psychic pain and geographic transience, trying to analyze your dreams, reading books by intense women drunk in the bathtub. It’s about the desire to glean something useful and transcendent out of a period of feeling unknown to yourself, stoking the faith that some force could grab you by your collar and pull you back into your own life.”

Watch the video, directed by Ella Sinskey, below.

entry.summary: Deerlady, the hypnotic indie rock duo who were a Stereogum Band To Watch in 2024, are no more. Guitarist Magdalena Abrego, one half of the duo, announced that she was leaving earlier this year. Today, Abrego releases the new album Xolo, her first-ever solo release. It’s an experimental mood-piece of a record that works as…
entry.content:
Deerlady, the hypnotic indie rock duo who were a Stereogum Band To Watch in 2024, are no more. Guitarist Magdalena Abrego, one half of the duo, announced that she was leaving earlier this year. Today, Abrego releases the new album Xolo, her first-ever solo release. It's an experimental mood-piece of a record that works as a kind of conceptual piece about loss.

The title Xolo is not a play on the word "solo." Instead, the album is named after the xoloitzcuintli, a dog breed that represents the process of moving into the afterlife in Mexican culture. Abego grew up with immigrant parents in Chicago, and she went on to study guitar performance at the New England Conservatory of Music before becoming a faculty member there. Abrego recorded the album in Brooklyn, and it's got her on vocals, guitar, synth, electronics, and ocarina, as well as some very personal field recordings. Only two other musicians appear: bass clarinetist Allison Burik and pianist Sonya Belaya. Here's what Abrego says about the album:

Lately, I look around and notice all the quiet ways that our ability to foster deep connection is at threat, especially as we are encouraged to embrace individualism, understand ourselves as self-sufficient, and accept displacement as inevitable, as though being uprooted were simply another condition of modern life. I’ve begun to believe that connection is not something we inherit; it is something we have to practice, protect, and even fight to keep.

For me, processing what I’ve been through so publicly feels like an act of rebellion against the structures that encourage us to carry our suffering alone. What I know now is that there is a kind of power in looking backward to understand the ones who came before us as not simply gone, but alive in the ways we show care, in the gestures we repeat without knowing where they began, and in what we choose to pass on. Perhaps survival is not simply making it through the darkness. Perhaps it is learning how to become a light that someone else, not yet here, will one day recognize.

Xolo is out in full today. Right now, its only available for purchase and streaming on Bandcamp. Check it out below.

entry.content:
My Chemical Romance have been enjoying the most beautiful victory lap. For the past few years, they've been celebrating and expanding the world of their third studio album, The Black Parade, which turned 20 last week. Today, they've released a short film titled Prelude To The End, a collaboration with visual artist Lauren Tsai.

The film fuses Tsai's own visual universe The Dying World, which she debuted as a short film at the 2025 Annecy Film Festival, with My Chemical Romance's intricate mythology. It's soundtracked by The Black Parade's opening song, "The End," and features a remarkable voice cast. Tsai voices the protagonist Astrid, alongside Billie Eilish as Astrid's friend, Phoebe Bridgers as her sister, Hideo Kojima as the Teacher, and f as the Dean. The film also features a live recording of Pascal Dusapin's Flying River, Violin Concerto, performed by the Utopia Orchestra at Fondation Louis Vuitton, conducted by Giuseppe Mengoli, with Daniel Lozakovich on solo violin.

The story follows Astrid, a student at an eerie New England boarding school where some dark, weird shit is clearly going on. The school's faculty tries to silence Astrid's creativity? imagination? emotions? autonomy? by throwing away her sketchbook. Astrid goes after it, tumbling down a trash chute and into what the press release describes as "a world inhabited by forgotten ideas," where she's confronted with her own.

The film's opening shot introduces the school as Paper Academy. This is important: it could be a connection to The Paper Kingdom, the unfinished album My Chemical Romance were working on around the time the band broke up. Whether this is a deliberate reference, a breadcrumb pointing toward something new, or simply a name that fits the film's world remains unclear. But it's freaking exciting nonetheless. It's been a delight diving into Reddit threads.

My Chemical Romance are vying for their first-ever #1 album with the new The Black Parade reissue, which could top the chart if it outsells Olivia Rodrigo. Rodrigo also seems to be rooting for them; she posted from one of MCR's shows this week. The band will play their final Los Angeles shows this weekend — 10/30 and 10/31 — while Phoebe Bridgers is also in town for a Halloween merch pop-up. Bridgers released a live EP on Tidal yesterday, too, making her appearance in Prelude To The End feel like its all connected.

Prelude To The End will be screened ahead of My Chem's final LA dates at the Hollywood Bowl. Watch it below.

entry.content:
The Australian-born, New Zealand-based folk artist Jazmine Mary released the striking album I Want To Rock And Roll last year. Next month, she'll follow it up with a new LP called Country Milk. On Instagram, Mary writes that she made the album "in the space of a manic month with my loved ones," but lead single "Shower Beer" doesn't sound manic. Instead, it's a soft, tender folk song that features her peers Cass Basil and Vera Ellen. Mary directed their own video for the song, and it features Mary dancing in slo-mo with the actor Yvette Parsons. Check it out below.

02 "Bloodline
03 "You're A Good Man, Girl"

06 "Geese"
07 "Bend"

Country Milk is out 11/27.

entry.title: Lamb Rebrands As Lambb Following Complaint From Trip-Hop Duo, Shares New Single “OBSESSION”
entry.summary: Lamb the singer has shared a new single, "Obsession," and rebranded as Lambb following a complaint from the trip-hop duo of the same name.
entry.content:
When up-and-coming alt-pop singer Lamb announced her debut EP and tour earlier this year, fans of the now-defunct Manchester trip-hop duo Lamb were a bit confused. The latter released statements clarifying that they were not reuniting, attempting to get in touch with the other Lamb to resolve the issue, and thanking us for posting about the mix-up. You're welcome, Lamb!

Apparently, it worked, because Lamb the singer is now quietly rebranding as Lambb with an extra B. Although she released her previous single "TALK," which got a big boost when Jungkook of BTS used it in an Instagram post, under her original name last month, she's gradually been rolling out the new spelling on various platforms since then.

Today, Lambb is announcing a new EP called There's Someone In The Yard and releasing her first official song as Lambb. You can listen to "OBSESSION," a dark electronic pop track, and watch its accompanying music video below.

There's Someone In The Yard is out 11/20 via Warner.

entry.content:
The Aussie blokes did it. For Triple J's Like A Version, Tame Impala covered Seal's "Kiss From A Rose." Their spin on the Batman Forever Soundtrack standout feels both majestic and hypnotic. There's something Beach Boys-y about it, probably the harmonies. It's a deceivingly simple song. Kevin Parker described the childhood favorite as "quite proggy," given its unexpected rhythm changes.

"It wasn't an easy decision, if I'm honest," he explained. "A few of us had the idea simultaneously, and we were like, 'Ah yeah, we can't do that. That's too hard.' We just thought we weren't going to be able to do it. Once we accepted that none of us sound like Seal — none of us have the insane voice that he does — once we were content with it's us, it's a bunch of Aussie blokes doing it, then I think we were at peace with it. We're just gonna do the best we can."

They seem to have gotten the Seal of approval: Seal's Instagram account commented with hand-clapping emojis on Tame Impala's post, although the artist does outsource his social media activity. Tame Impala also performed their hit "Dracula." Watch both performances below.

entry.content:
Sadly, there will be no more live performances from the iconic, mysterious avant-garde musician Jandek. Yesterday, his longtime associate and Corwood Coordinator Sheila Smith posted the news via Instagram. The post read:

To everyone who has written to me regarding a Jandek show, thank you. Please be advised that there will be no more Jandek concerts. - Sheila Smith

The enigmatic, trailblazing Houston artist put out records for years, starting in the '70s, before playing his first-ever live show in 2004. Since then, his infrequent appearances have been intimate and frequently incredible, like the one he did in a cave in Upstate New York a couple years ago. The last show he played was Dec. 12, 2025 at the Orange Show in Houston, Texas.
